look_here_first: Confirm BULB-origin basal trifoliolate leaves and separate LEAFLESS flowering scapes. Examine the small, relatively shallow-notched leaflets (usually 8–15 mm, notch ~1/4–1/3 depth): OXALATE LINES along the notch margins help distinguish O. violacea from O. drummondii. Flower color is not a reliable separator.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Stemless bulbous perennial, basal leaves and separate leafless scapes.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Basal trifoliolate leaves; 3 obcordate leaflets commonly (5–)8–15(–20) mm, notch ~1/4–1/3 length; oxalate deposits/lines often evident along notch margins.

key_traits.label: Flowers
key_traits.text: Five petals, often pink to violet; flowering stems are leafless scapes, not leafy aerial stems. Inspect sepals and inflorescence, not just color.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Capsules produced on scapes; check mature fruit and bulb for positive ID.
